extracted.subtask_description: A collection of International/Chinese Mathematical Olympiad problems, solutions, and informational notes about IMO rules and procedures; meant as a reference for competitors and coaches. Contains problem statements, worked solutions, and descriptions of competition organization and marking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competition format and scoring
rubrics_metrics.description: The competition lasts for 2 days, and there are 3 problems to be completed within 4.5 hours each day. Each question is 7 marks which total up to 42 marks. The full score for a team is 252 marks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the timing and scoring parameters used to structure the contest and aggregate individual and team scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medal allocation and special awards
rubrics_metrics.description: About half of the participants will be awarded a medal, where 1/12 will be awarded a gold medal. The numbers of gold, silver, and bronze medals awarded are in the ratio of 1:2:3 approximately. In the case when a participant provides a better solution than the official answer, a special award is given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The jury determines cut-off points for medals (see jury responsibilities). The approximate ratios and the special award policy guide recognition of performance beyond standard medal thresholds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Team delegation composition requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: All participating countries are required to send a delegation consisting of a leader, a deputy leader and 6 contestants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies the official composition of a national delegation eligible to participate and to perform leader/deputy marking duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem contribution, selection and translation process
rubrics_metrics.description: The problems are contributed by the participating countries and are later selected carefully by the host country for submission to the international jury set up by the host country. The host country does not provide any question. The problems are translated in working languages and the team leaders will translate them into their own languages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes provenance (participating countries), selection (host country curates submissions for the jury), and translation responsibilities (host produces working-language translations; team leaders handle translation into their native language).

rubrics_metrics.name: Marking process for answer scripts
rubrics_metrics.description: The answer scripts of each participating team will be marked by the team leader and the deputy leader. The team leader will later present them to the coordinators for assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Team leaders/deputies perform initial marking of their team’s scripts; coordinators (appointed by the organizers) review these marks as part of the standard marking/coordination workflow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jury formation and responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The jury is formed by the various team leaders and an appointed chairman by the host country. The jury is responsible for deciding the final 6 problems, finalizing the marking standard, ensuring the accuracy of the translation of the problems, standardizing replies to written queries raised by participants during the competition, synchronizing differences in marking between the leaders and the coordinators and deciding on the cut-off points for the medals depending on the contestants' results as the difficulties of problems each year are different.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies who composes the jury and enumerates its core duties: final problem selection, setting/standardizing marking schemes, translation accuracy checks, handling participant queries, reconciling marking discrepancies, and determining medal cutoffs.
